option_description: Whether secret/restricted PSP keys (sk_*/rk_*) are kept out of client bundles, mobile apps, and committed source — only the publishable key (pk_) ever appears client-side.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Leaked or over-privileged API key" (MITRE T1552) — fires when false, i.e. a secret/restricted key is found in shipped client code or the repository, letting an attacker call the PSP API as us.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep the client bundle and committed source for live/test secret and restricted key prefixes.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No matches in client bundles / committed source (secure). Any match of sk_*/rk_* in shipped client code is a critical exposure.
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Best practices for managing secret API keys

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a pre-commit hook / secret scanner rejects sk_/rk_ patterns and that CI/CD pipelines are audited periodically.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Pre-commit hook / secret scanner rejects commits containing sk_/rk_ patterns; CI/CD pipelines audited periodically (secure) vs no scanning (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Best practices for managing secret API keys

option_description: Whether integrations use restricted least-privilege keys (rk_live_) scoped to minimal per-resource permissions rather than one unrestricted full-access secret key.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Leaked or over-privileged API key" (T1552) — fires when false (a single unrestricted secret key is shared across integrations), so a compromised key has unbounded blast radius.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Open the Stripe Dashboard API key listing and inspect whether keys are restricted with explicit per-resource scopes.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Restricted keys with explicit per-resource scopes (secure) vs only an unrestricted secret key (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Restricted API keys

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the integration's key inventory to confirm each component uses a restricted key scoped to the minimal permissions it needs (e.g. read-only for a dispute monitor).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Per-component restricted keys with least-privilege scopes documented (secure) vs a shared unrestricted full-access secret key (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Restricted API keys

option_description: Whether secret/restricted PSP keys are resolved at runtime from a secrets vault (AWS/GCP Secret Manager, Azure Key Vault, HashiCorp Vault) with access audit logging, rather than hard-coded or in plaintext config.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Leaked or over-privileged API key" (T1552) — fires when false (keys hard-coded or committed in plaintext), exposing the credential at rest in VCS or config.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm keys are injected from a vault/secret manager at runtime and never hard-coded, in committed config, or exposed on error pages / diagnostic output.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Keys injected from a vault/secret manager (secure); never hard-coded; never exposed on error pages or diagnostic output.
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Best practices for managing secret API keys

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect deployment/runtime config and environment wiring to confirm the key value is a vault reference (secret ARN / vault path), not a literal sk_/rk_ value.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Config references a secret-manager path/ARN resolved at boot (secure) vs a literal sk_*/rk_* value embedded in config (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether a documented, practiced key-rotation process exists — keys rotated periodically and immediately on suspected exposure, using the delayed-expiration rollover window.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Leaked or over-privileged API key" (T1552) — fires when false (long-lived static keys never rotated, no contingency plan), extending the useful life of a leaked key.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the written rotation procedure and evidence of periodic rotation plus immediate rotation on suspected exposure.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Written rotation procedure + evidence of periodic rotation (secure). Stripe also proactively notifies/deactivates keys it detects as exposed.
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Best practices for managing secret API keys

option_description: Whether test/sandbox keys (sk_test_/pk_test_) are kept out of production and live keys out of non-prod, preventing real-charge accidents and cross-environment data leakage.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Leaked or over-privileged API key" (T1552) — fires when false (live keys appear in dev/test, or test keys deployed to prod).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review Stripe Dashboard request logs / API request logs to confirm live-mode keys are used only from production contexts.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Live-mode keys used only from prod (secure); audit logs for live keys appearing in non-prod contexts (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Best practices for managing secret API keys

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect per-environment configuration to confirm prod resolves a live key and non-prod resolves a test key.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Prod config resolves sk_live_/rk_live_, non-prod resolves sk_test_ (secure) vs mixed environments (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether every inbound webhook is verified with the Stripe-Signature header (t=,v1=HMAC-SHA256) against the whsec_ endpoint signing secret via constructEvent/construct_event over the RAW request body before any handling.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Forged or unverified webhook events" (MITRE T1190) — fires when false, letting an attacker POST forged payment_intent.succeeded events to trigger order fulfilment without payment.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the handler calls construct_event/constructEvent(rawBody, sigHeader, endpointSecret) and rejects on failure, with the raw UTF-8 body passed unmodified (Express: route mounted before express.json()).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Handler calls Stripe::Webhook.construct_event / Webhook.constructEvent(rawBody, sigHeader, endpointSecret) and rejects on failure (secure). Raw body must be UTF-8 unmodified.
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Resolve webhook signature verification errors

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep the webhook code path for the verification call and signature header handling.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Webhook route invokes signature verification with the whsec_ endpoint secret (secure) vs no verification call present (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Receive Stripe events in your webhook endpoint

option_description: Whether the webhook endpoint is served over HTTPS/TLS only (https:// URL), rejecting plaintext http:// delivery.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Forged or unverified webhook events" (T1190) — fires when false (plaintext http:// endpoint), so forged/tampered events can be injected over cleartext and signature material observed in transit.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Open the registered webhook endpoint in the Stripe Dashboard and confirm the configured URL is https://.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configured webhook URL is https:// (secure) vs http:// (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Integration security guide (webhooks must use TLS)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe the webhook endpoint over plaintext HTTP to confirm it does not accept cleartext delivery.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Plaintext HTTP is refused or redirected to HTTPS (secure) vs the endpoint accepting POSTs over http:// (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether inbound webhook traffic is restricted to the PSP's published source IP ranges as defence-in-depth alongside signature verification.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Forged or unverified webhook events" (T1190) — fires when false (endpoint accepts POSTs from any source IP), widening the surface for forged-event delivery.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the firewall/WAF/ingress rule fronting the webhook endpoint to confirm it restricts inbound traffic to the PSP's published IP ranges.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Allow rule scoped to the PSP's documented webhook source IP ranges (secure) vs open to 0.0.0.0/0 (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the documented PSP source-IP ranges are tracked and kept current as the provider publishes changes.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Maintained allowlist matching the PSP's current published webhook IP ranges (secure) vs no IP restriction (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Integration security guide

option_description: Whether webhook signature verification enforces the library default ~5-minute (300s) timestamp recency window so intercepted-and-replayed signed events are rejected by staleness; tolerance=0 disables the check.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Webhook replay attack" (MITRE T1080) — fires when false (tolerance=0 or no timestamp check), so a captured valid signed event can be replayed indefinitely.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the signature-verification call to confirm it uses the library default 5-minute (300s) tolerance and is never set to 0.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Signature verification uses the library default 5-minute tolerance (timestamp is part of the signed payload) (secure). A tolerance of 0 disables the recency check (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Receive Stripe events in your webhook endpoint (replay attacks / tolerance)

option_description: Whether the webhook handler deduplicates on event.id before applying side effects, so a re-sent (replayed or Stripe-retried) event with a previously-processed id does not double-apply fulfilment.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Webhook replay attack" (T1080) — fires when false (no dedup), so replays/retries re-apply effects.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm in the Stripe Dashboard that the endpoint URL is HTTPS and review that the handler design deduplicates on event.id given Stripe's automatic retries.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Handler records processed event.id and skips duplicates on Stripe's automatic retries (secure) vs a non-idempotent handler (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Integration security guide (webhooks must use TLS)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the handler code/data store to confirm processed event.id values are recorded and duplicates are skipped before applying side effects.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Processed event.id persisted and checked before side effects (secure) vs no dedup store (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Receive Stripe events in your webhook endpoint

option_description: Whether card data is tokenized client-side via Stripe.js/Elements/Checkout (or equivalent hosted fields) using the publishable key, so only a PaymentMethod/token (pm_/tok_) ever reaches our server.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Cardholder data exposure / PCI scope creep" (MITRE T1005) — fires when false (raw PAN posted to / handled by our servers), pulling our environment into full PCI scope (SAQ-D, 300+ controls).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the payment form uses Stripe Elements iframes / Checkout and that server endpoints receive PaymentMethod IDs, not card numbers.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Payment form uses Stripe Elements iframes / Checkout; server endpoints receive PaymentMethod IDs not card numbers (secure). Any code path accepting a raw PAN (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Integration security guide / Scoping considerations

option_description: Whether full PAN (and CVV/track data) is never persisted at rest — only non-sensitive Stripe-returned data (last4, brand, expiry) is stored.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Cardholder data exposure / PCI scope creep" (T1005) — fires when false (full card data stored at rest), violating PCI DSS Req 3.4 and creating a breach target.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the data inventory and persisted stores to confirm only tokens + last4/brand/expiry are stored and no full PAN/CVV/track data is retained.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Data inventory shows only tokens + last4/brand/exp stored, with documented retention/residency controls (secure).
how_to_obtain.source: PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 3 — Protect Stored Account Data (corpus)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Scan persisted data stores / backups for 13–16 digit PAN-shaped strings that are not masked.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No unmasked full PANs at rest (secure). PCI Req 3.4 requires PAN rendered unreadable.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether full PAN and sensitive authentication data never appear in application, access, or audit logs (logs masked to last4/****).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Cardholder data exposure / PCI scope creep" (T1005) — fires when false (PAN/SAD written to logs), violating PCI DSS Req 3.4 / Req 10.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep application/access logs for unmasked 13–16 digit PAN-shaped strings.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No full PANs in logs (secure). PCI Req 3.4 requires PAN rendered unreadable; Req 10 requires audit logs that themselves must not leak CHD.
how_to_obtain.source: PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 3 — Protect Stored Account Data (corpus)

option_description: Whether persisted account data (tokens plus any stored cardholder metadata) is encrypted at rest via managed KMS/SSE rather than stored in plaintext.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Cardholder data exposure / PCI scope creep" (T1005) — secondary trigger reinforcing the PCI data-protection facet; fires when false (stored payment data in plaintext, PCI DSS Req 3).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm persisted account data stores use managed encryption at rest (KMS/SSE) and document the key management approach.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Stored tokens and cardholder metadata encrypted at rest via managed KMS/SSE (secure) vs plaintext storage (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 3 — Protect Stored Account Data (corpus)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the storage backend's encryption configuration (e.g. cloud provider describe call) to confirm encryption-at-rest is enabled.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Encryption-at-rest reported enabled with a managed/customer-managed key (secure) vs disabled (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether all server-to-PSP API calls and payment pages are made over TLS/HTTPS only, with no plaintext HTTP fallback or downgrade path.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "TLS downgrade / MITM on PSP transport" (MITRE T1557) — fires when false (any cleartext HTTP call to the PSP API), exposing tokens, credentials, and transaction data in motion.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the TLS handshake against the PSP API endpoint succeeds over TLS and inspect the certificate validity dates.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: TLS 1.2+ handshake succeeds against a valid cert chain (secure). Stripe requires TLS 1.2 or above; verify with Qualys SSL Labs SSL Server Test.
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Integration security guide (TLS 1.2 or above)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep the integration source for any http:// PSP endpoint URLs indicating a plaintext fallback.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No plaintext http:// PSP URLs (secure) vs any cleartext HTTP call to the PSP (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether the HTTP client / TLS stack negotiating with the PSP permits TLS versions below 1.2 (TLS 1.0/1.1 or SSLv3). Secure value is false.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "TLS downgrade / MITM on PSP transport" (T1557) — fires when true (a downgrade to weak/deprecated TLS is possible), exposing transaction data to interception.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt a deprecated-protocol handshake to confirm TLS <1.2 is refused, then confirm TLS 1.2+ succeeds.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: TLS 1.0/1.1/SSLv3 handshake is refused (secure: weak versions disabled). Stripe requires TLS 1.2 or above.
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Integration security guide (TLS 1.2 or above)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the HTTP client / TLS stack configuration for the minimum protocol setting permitting sub-1.2 versions.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Client minimum protocol is TLS 1.2+ (secure, attribute=false) vs config permitting TLS 1.0/1.1/SSLv3 (insecure, attribute=true).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: The minimum TLS protocol version the connection to the PSP API will negotiate (SSLv3 / TLSv1.0 / TLSv1.1 / TLSv1.2 / TLSv1.3). PSPs mandate TLS 1.2 or above.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "TLS downgrade / MITM on PSP transport" (T1557) — fires on a weak floor (SSLv3 / TLSv1.0 / TLSv1.1); TLSv1.2/TLSv1.3 floors stay silent.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the TLS client's configured minimum protocol version for the PSP connection.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A floor of SSLv3 / TLSv1.0 / TLSv1.1 is insecure; TLSv1.2 or TLSv1.3 is secure.
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Integration security guide (TLS 1.2 or above)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate accepted TLS versions against the PSP endpoint to corroborate the negotiated floor.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only TLSv1.2/TLSv1.3 offered (secure) vs TLSv1.0/TLSv1.1/SSLv3 present (insecure floor).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether the HTTP client validates the PSP API server's certificate chain and hostname (no verify=False / rejectUnauthorized:false / disabled hostname verification).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "TLS downgrade / MITM on PSP transport" (T1557) — fires when false: disabled certificate verification lets an adversary-in-the-middle present a forged cert and intercept tokens and transaction data.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the HTTP client configuration for disabled certificate or hostname verification.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: HTTP client does not disable certificate verification (no verify=False / rejectUnauthorized:false) (secure) vs verification disabled (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Integration security guide

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep the integration source for common certificate-verification-disabling flags.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No matches (secure) vs any verification-disabling flag present in the PSP client path (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether every mutating charge/PaymentIntent POST sends a unique Idempotency-Key header (V4 UUID or order/cart-derived) so network-error retries return the saved first response instead of creating a second charge.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Double-charge / amount tampering via missing integrity controls" (MITRE T1565) — fires when false (no idempotency key, retries can double-charge).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep the integration source for the Idempotency-Key header being set on charge/PaymentIntent POSTs.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: POST/charge calls set an Idempotency-Key (secure). Stripe also errors if a reused key carries different params, preventing accidental misuse.
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Idempotent requests (API reference)

option_description: Whether the charge amount and currency are computed and authoritatively set server-side from trusted catalog/order data rather than echoed from the client request.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Double-charge / amount tampering via missing integrity controls" (T1565) — fires when false (amount/currency taken from a client-trusted value), enabling amount/currency tampering.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the PaymentIntent/charge amount and currency are recomputed server-side from the order record, not echoed from the client request.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: PaymentIntent/charge amount is recomputed server-side from the order record (secure) vs amount echoed from the client request (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — The Payment Intents API (server-side integration)

option_description: Whether the server independently verifies the order total against trusted order/catalog records before charging, never trusting a client-supplied total.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Double-charge / amount tampering via missing integrity controls" (T1565) — fires when false (no server-side order-total verification), letting a buyer pay an attacker-chosen amount.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the checkout/charge path to confirm the server independently recomputes/validates the order total against trusted order/catalog records before charging.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Server recomputes the total from trusted order/catalog data before charging (secure) vs a client-supplied total used to charge (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — The Payment Intents API (server-side integration)

option_description: Whether 3D Secure 2 / PSD2 Strong Customer Authentication is enforced on in-scope card payments via the PaymentIntents flow (handling the 3DS next_action) rather than raw charge APIs that bypass authentication.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Payment fraud via missing SCA / 3DS" (MITRE T1583) — fires when false (SCA/3DS2 not enforced), enabling card-not-present / stolen-card fraud and merchant-borne chargebacks.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the payment flow uses PaymentIntents and handles the 3DS next_action, so Stripe's mandatory-authentication rules run regardless of manual request.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Payment flow uses PaymentIntents and handles the 3DS next_action; Stripe's mandatory-authentication rules run regardless of manual request (secure).
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — 3D Secure authentication / Strong Customer Authentication readiness

option_description: Whether active fraud/abuse controls — a risk rules engine plus velocity/anomaly checks (Radar-style risk rules) — are enabled for the integration, with a defined dispute/chargeback workflow.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Payment fraud via missing SCA / 3DS" (T1583) — fires when false (no fraud/velocity/anomaly detection), leaving stolen-card and abusive patterns undetected.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the Stripe Dashboard confirm fraud-prevention (Radar) rules are configured and disputes are monitored.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Fraud-prevention rules configured and disputes monitored (secure). A read-only restricted key may be issued to a third-party dispute monitor rather than a full key.
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Restricted API keys / Best practices

option_description: Whether SCA exemptions (low-value, TRA, frictionless / Data Only) are applied deliberately and narrowly with appropriate liability handling, rather than broad/blanket exemptions that suppress mandated authentication.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Payment fraud via missing SCA / 3DS" (T1583) — fires when false (exemptions improperly broad or misapplied), undermining SCA coverage.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review how SCA exemptions are requested in the integration to confirm they are scoped (low-value, TRA, frictionless/Data-Only) with proper liability handling, not blanket.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Exemptions used deliberately and narrowly with documented liability handling (secure) vs broad blanket exemptions suppressing required SCA (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — 3D Secure authentication / Strong Customer Authentication readiness

option_description: Whether client authentication to the PSP integration uses OAuth2 client-credentials or mTLS-bound (RFC 8705) short-lived, least-privilege access tokens rather than a long-lived static shared bearer secret/API key.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Trusted-relationship abuse of the PSP integration" (MITRE T1199) — fires when false (long-lived static credentials are the trust anchor), so a single credential compromise grants durable, unbounded access.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm token acquisition uses OAuth2 client credentials or mTLS certificate-bound access tokens with short TTL per RFC 8705.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Token acquisition uses client credentials / mTLS certificate-bound access tokens with short TTL (secure) per RFC 8705.
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 8705 — OAuth 2.0 Mutual-TLS Client Authentication (corpus)

option_description: Whether the secret/restricted keys (or token endpoints) for the PSP integration are bound to a NAT-gateway / reserved source-IP allowlist so a stolen credential is unusable from an attacker network.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Trusted-relationship abuse of the PSP integration" (T1199 / T1078) — fires when false (credential usable from any source IP), removing a network constraint on trusted-relationship abuse.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Stripe Dashboard key settings to confirm an IP allowlist is configured for the secret/restricted key.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Stripe Dashboard > Developers > API keys (key settings)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Dashboard key settings show IP allowlist configured for the key (secure) vs no IP restriction (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Best practices for managing secret API keys

option_description: Whether access granted to/through the PSP integration follows least privilege — scoped restricted keys (rk_live_) with minimal per-resource permissions rather than a single unrestricted full-access secret key.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for both "Trusted-relationship abuse of the PSP integration" (T1199) and "Leaked or over-privileged API key" (T1552) — fires when false (over-broad permissions on the trusted PSP connection), widening blast radius.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the Stripe Dashboard API key listing to confirm keys are restricted with minimal per-resource scopes, not a single unrestricted secret key.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Restricted keys with explicit per-resource scopes (secure) vs only an unrestricted secret key (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Restricted API keys

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the granted scopes map to only the operations each component legitimately requires.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each integration's key scopes match its minimal required operations (secure) vs over-broad grants (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Best practices for managing secret API keys

option_description: Whether the trust/permission scope specifically granted on the PSP connection (Connect account scopes, restricted-key resource grants, webhook/event subscriptions) is constrained to only the financial operations this component requires.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Trusted-relationship abuse of the PSP integration" (T1199) — fires when false (over-broad trust scope), so abuse can pivot into financial operations beyond the component's legitimate need.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the PSP connection's Connect scopes, restricted-key resource grants, and webhook/event subscriptions to confirm they are limited to the financial operations this component needs.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Trust scope (Connect scopes / restricted-key grants / event subscriptions) constrained to required financial operations (secure) vs over-broad scope (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Stripe — Restricted API keys

option_description: Whether a complete, time-synced audit trail of payment operations and PSP webhook events is recorded per PCI DSS Req 10 (without storing CHD).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Transaction-data exfiltration over the PSP channel without audit trail" (MITRE T1567) — fires when false, so exfiltration over the trusted PSP HTTPS channel leaves no record.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm audit logs record payment operations and webhook event IDs with retention and alerting per PCI Req 10, masked and excluding PAN.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Audit logs record payment operations and webhook event IDs with retention and alerting per PCI Req 10 (secure); logs are masked and exclude PAN.
how_to_obtain.source: PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 10 — Log and Monitor All Access (corpus)

option_description: Whether anomaly/alerting is active on PSP API request logs and webhook events (unusual volume, off-hours bulk reads, residency drift).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Transaction-data exfiltration over the PSP channel without audit trail" (T1567) — fires when false, so attacker pulls of customer/transaction data blend with normal traffic and trigger no alert.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm alerting rules exist on PSP API request logs and webhook events for unusual volume, off-hours bulk reads, and residency drift.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Active anomaly alerting on PSP API/webhook traffic (secure) vs no detection — exfiltration blends with normal traffic (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 10 — Log and Monitor All Access (corpus)

option_description: The retention period (in days) for transaction/audit logs. PCI DSS Req 10 requires audit history retained for at least one year (365 days).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Transaction-data exfiltration over the PSP channel without audit trail" (T1567) — fires when < 365, making investigation of slow exfiltration over the PSP channel impossible.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the configured retention period for transaction/audit logs (days) in the log pipeline / SIEM configuration.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Retention >= 365 days (secure, PCI Req 10); a value below 365 is insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 10 — Log and Monitor All Access (corpus)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the log store / retention-policy API to confirm the effective retention window in days.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Effective retention reported as >= 365 days (secure) vs < 365 (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether regulated transaction-data residency and retention obligations are documented and enforced (data pinned to permitted jurisdictions; only tokenized references + non-sensitive metadata retained).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Transaction-data exfiltration over the PSP channel without audit trail" (T1567) — fires when false, so data-residency drift moves regulated transaction data outside permitted jurisdictions undetected.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the data inventory and residency controls to confirm only tokens + last4/brand/exp are stored with documented retention/residency obligations.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Data inventory shows only tokens + last4/brand/exp stored, with documented retention/residency controls (secure).
how_to_obtain.source: PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 3 — Protect Stored Account Data (corpus) / Stripe Integration security guide
